chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on him) told me, saying: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated to me via an upraised chain from Muhammad ibn Qays and Aamir ibn al-Samt, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said:

On the Day of Resurrection, a people will come wearing garments of light, with light upon their faces, recognized by the marks of prostration. They will step over row after row until they stand before the Lord of the worlds. The prophets, angels, martyrs, and righteous people will envy them. Umar ibn al-Khattab asked him: 'Who are these, O Messenger of Allah, whom the prophets, angels, martyrs, and righteous people will envy?' He said: 'They are our Shia, and Ali is their Imam.'
ai.seo_question: Who are the people envied by prophets and angels on the Day of Judgment according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Sadu by Shaykh al-Saduq in *Fadail al-Shia*, this hadith highlights the eschatological honor of the *Shi'a* as a distinct community identified by the physical marks of devotion and divine light. It underscores the concept of *Wala'* (loyalty) to Imam Ali as the defining characteristic that elevates them above prophets and angels in status, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on their unique spiritual lineage.

en.badr-shahin: Mohammed bin al-Hasan bin Ahmed bin al-Waleed (r) related to me from Mohammed bin al-Hasan as-Saffar… from Mohammed bin Qays and Aamir bin as-Simt that Abu Ja’far (a) related that the Prophet (s) said:

"On the Day of Resurrection, some people dressing clothes of light with luminous faces whom will be identified by the signs of prostration will come. They will overstep the rows until they stand in front of the Lord of the worlds. The prophets, angels, shahids, and righteous people will envy them." Omar bin al-Khattab asked: "O Allah’s Messenger, who are they whom the prophets, angels, shahids, and righteous men will envy?" The Prophet (s) answered: "They will be our Shia, and Ali will be their imam."
